properties.description: Construction of the Chelan Wet Weather Storage Tank located at 4034 West Marginal Way SW. There will be a new above-grade 4,995-sf one-story facility building (approx. 111-ft x 45-ft) with a concrete slab foundation on structural fill that will include: a 1,400-sf generator room (approx. 25-ft x 56-ft), a 1,258-sf electrical room (approx. 17-ft x 74-ft), a 48-sf restroom (approx. 6-ft x 8-ft), a 240-sf communication room (approx. 15-ft x 16-ft), and a 1,247-sf C2 room (approx. 29-ft x 43-ft) with a utility area, hydropneumatics tank, C2 booster pumps, tipping bucket valves, and air gap tank. A new above grade 2,250-sf architecturally screened odor control area (approx. 50-ft x 45-ft) with a concrete slab foundation on structural fill that will include: architectural screening (approx. 10-ft in height), dual bed scrubber, enclosed fan, filter, raised platform, and roof access. A new above-grade 4,200-sf one-story tipping bucket enclosure (approx. 300-ft x 13-ft) with a concrete slab foundation on structural fill. The new building footprint areas total 11,445-sf (facility building, screened odor control area, and tipping bucket enclosure). New at-grade impervious pavement areas and landscaping that include: an 11,514-sf fire apparatus road, a 3,857-sf maintenance access road, and 1,143-sf of parking with 6 stalls total (2 EV and 4 for maintenance). A new 7,078-sf stormwater bioretention cell providing water quality and infiltration for targeted surfaces and 1,066 linear feet of new fencing to include 2 new vehicular access gates. A new below-grade 37,500-sf, 7 MG storage tank (approx. 300-ft x 125-ft) with structural fill foundation material and associated channels and mechanical facilities that include: five flushing channels, a collection channel, and pump sump. There will be new access hatches (4 total) and a new 288-sf drain pump vault (approx. 12-ft x 24-ft). The new construction areas total is 68,950-sf with new and replaced impervious surfaces totaling 66,570-sf with total site excavation of 81,900-cy.

properties.description: The proposed medical facility development consists of redeveloping the site of the existing building with a new two-story, 11,400 SF free-standing emergency department and urgent care facility. This facility is outpatient only and primarily provides clinical related treatment and diagnostic services. It does not operate as a nursing home or hospital and does not offer overnight medical or surgical care. It will be open 24/7 and have ambulance/service access to the building. Services offered within the building on the first floor will include CT, X-ray, Lab, and both emergent and urgent care exams/treatment. The second floor will consist of staff, support, and maintenance areas. The building will also have 26-27 parking spaces (which is in line with city requirements), direct access to public transportation route, a backup emergency generator with 96-hour run time, direct road access from all three roads along the parcel, and vertical circulation between the ambulance entrance and the two levels will be handled with a patient stretcher sized elevator. Two exit stairs will be included as fire exits with one or both accessing the first floor for staff access.

properties.description: The King County Wastewater Treatment Division (WTD) proposes to install a new, permanent generator to replace the existing portable generator at the Alki Wet Weather Treatment Station Facility (WWTSF) located within King County Parcel 0148000274 at 3350 Beach Drive SW. The new generator will function as a standby generator for both the Alki WWTSF and the 63rd Avenue Pump Station at 3535 Beach Drive SW, Seattle. In the event of a utility outage, power from this standby generator located at the Alki WWTSF will run the 63rd Avenue Pump Station Facility pumps. The project will involve trenching and laying electrical duct within the public road right of way between these two WTD facilities. As the duct approaches the Pump Station, it will cross several existing utilities under the southern sidewalk of Beach Drive. The 2" gas line utility cannot be avoided at this location. As such, WTD is requesting to relocate a section of this gas line to accommodate the duct.
